caption:
Business Today reported in August that 66% of Indian AI and ML workers expect job cuts within three to six months. Engineers were the least worried group in that survey.

That is the part worth sitting with. The people closest to the work assume their output will speak for them. It used to. The reporting now says top performers are not insulated either.

The contract many of you signed with yourself was simple: deliver well, stay safe, get recognised. That contract is being rewritten without your signature.

In command, competence was assumed. It was the floor, not the achievement. What separated officers was whether the room knew where they stood when a decision had to be made.

So learn to be seen. Hold the room when you speak. Let a pause do work your words cannot. Say the thing once, clearly, before someone else says it louder.

Visibility is no longer polish. It is protection.
alt_text: A plain dark text card. Bold white type reads: Competence was never the achievement. It was the floor. Below it, in smaller type, the words Lumina Presence.

topic.title: AI layoffs break the competence-equals-security contract
topic.angle: This audience's entire strategy has been "be excellent and it will be recognised" — and the evidence now says delivery no longer buys safety, making visibility and influence a survival skill rather than a nice-to-have.
topic.why_now: A sustained run of Indian coverage since mid-summer — Outlook India on AI layoffs reshaping the IT workforce (20 Jul), Business Today arguing even top performers are no longer safe (6 Aug) and reporting 66% of Indian AI/ML workers expect cuts within 3–6 months while engineers stay least worried (10 Aug) — is still unresolved and pairs naturally with the live appraisal cycle.

rationale: A stark, text-only card matches the blunt authority of the message and keeps the focus on the single hard claim about competence no longer buying safety.
